terminal.name: Device Terminal Workbench
terminal.description: Persistent Shell, SSH, Telnet, TCP, UDP, and serial workbenches with TLS relay and X11. Aide can read screenshots and video frames extracted by timestamp.
dependencies: Aide 0.1.18.0 RC3 or newer, trusted workbench identity, private session state and sessionCopyVersion=1 host context; graphics need a host implementing workbench.viewer.protocol=1 (aide main def8df6a or later). Plugin-only updates cannot add host capabilities.
Node.js 24, Linux Python 3 PTY/memfd, /bin/bash, and OpenSSH. The package includes ssh2 1.17.0, serialport 12.0.0, and runtime dependencies.
Serial testing used a native-driver virtual PTY. Real USB/UART requires device mapping and permissions; hardware and Windows/macOS were not tested.
Manually deployed device relays require Python 3.10+ and cryptography; serial relays also require pyserial 3.5. Fixed relay TCP ports must be reachable from the Aide runtime.
Built-in graphical windows for direct and relay SSH use a session-specific X Server allocated by Aide. Remote sshd must allow X11Forwarding and provide xauth.

Built-in graphical sessions need host-provided Xvfb, xauth, openbox, x11vnc and websockify in the Aide runtime image; the plugin does not install system packages. Linux is verified; macOS/Windows graphical hosts are not tested.
History restoration after workspace-mapping changes requires a host containing Aide PR #939. Existing sessions and logs remain workspace-specific; plugin upgrades cannot replace an older host.
Aide versions with shared workbench windows provide standalone graphical windows. Older hosts use the original graphics entry and can display it beside the terminal if the browser blocks pop-ups.
X11 capture requires Pillow XCB and WebP support in the Linux Aide runtime; the official Aide image already includes them.
terminal.permissions: Shell and SSH commands, SFTP transfers, TCP/UDP/serial sending, proxying, simulation, replay, and boundary-packet probing all require explicit user intent. Trusted Node plugins use the Aide runtime user’s permissions. Sensitive output or device echoes may also enter logs.
terminal.trustNotice: Requires paired Aide 0.1.18.0 RC3 or newer. Graphical panes additionally require a host with workbench.viewer.protocol=1 and Linux Xvfb/x11vnc/openbox/websockify. Relay copies share the configured target and relay key but have independent connections, PTYs and logs. Upgrading/stopping disconnects sessions, without replay or automatic reconnection. Base64 relay configuration backups contain the relay key and must be kept private. Loading fills a draft only; users initiate connections after saving. With built-in graphical windows for direct or relay SSH, remote applications can access that session’s dedicated display—connect only to trusted devices. Remote clipboard transfer requires manual copying. External DISPLAY or custom Xauthority uses restricted forwarding. Previously deployed relay scripts remain usable. Echo push requires a capable Aide host; older hosts continue polling.
